subtopic: Share Class Fees and Investment Returns
source_evidence: This means that owning a different class of the same fund will result in different investment returns. The effect of different fees on different mutual fund share classes is compounded over time.
question: Misconception: Because different share classes of the same mutual fund invest in the same portfolio, they must have identical investment returns.
answer: Different share classes can have different fees and expenses even though they invest in the same portfolio. Those cost differences can lead to different investment returns, and the effect of the fees compounds over time.
